task_instance: Produce Terraform Registry documentation for a minimal sample provider resource `example_widget`: write precise schema field descriptions (Go schema source), add an example HCL file under examples/resources/example_widget/resource.tf, add a docs/resources/example_widget.md.tmpl template referencing that example and the schema-generated markdown block, then run tfplugindocs (via `go generate ./...` or `go run github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-docs/cmd/tfplugindocs generate`) to produce the final docs/resources/example_widget.md that Terraform Registry actually publishes, and verify that generated file is correct.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is the *generated* Terraform Registry markdown page, produced by running the tfplugindocs generator (`go generate ./...` or `go run github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-docs/cmd/tfplugindocs generate --provider-name <name>`) against the Go schema source and the .md.tmpl template. This is step 4 of the skill's own workflow and is not optional cosmetic tooling -- tfplugindocs is what parses the schema struct, resolves Required/Optional/Computed/default semantics, injects the SchemaMarkdown block, and validates/renders the tffile-included HCL example. This runtime cannot run any code, script, or shell command (no Go toolchain, no `go run`/`go generate`), so the generator cannot be executed. I could hand-write a markdown file that merely imitates tfplugindocs' output format, but that would not be the skill's actual deliverable (schema-derived, tool-generated, and re-verifiable on every schema change) -- it would just be prose I made up, which defeats the entire purpose of the workflow (keeping docs mechanically in sync with schema) and could not be verified as accurate against the real schema types/plan-modifiers. I was able to complete the earlier, text-only steps (schema descriptions, example file, template file) but the run/verify step is a hard blocker.
